subject.title: RFC: Consolidate approval flow behind an ApprovalService port

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a core `ApprovalService`/adapter architecture, or keep approval ownership distributed and target only demonstrated lifecycle defects?
rationale: The request introduces a broad core abstraction and potentially durable API boundary; source-level failure evidence and repository-owner intent are needed before choosing that direction.

options.title: Request a scoped design
options.body: Ask for a current-source map, one demonstrated cross-module lifecycle defect, ownership boundaries, and an incremental migration plan before accepting a core service direction.

options.title: Retain distributed ownership
options.body: Keep the existing boundaries and invite a narrower issue or PR only when a concrete approval lifecycle invariant is broken.

options.title: Sponsor the service refactor
options.body: Assign an owner to define the core versus plugin/channel contract and stage the migration behind focused compatibility tests.

recommendation.title: Request a scoped design
recommendation.body: Ask for a current-source map, one demonstrated cross-module lifecycle defect, ownership boundaries, and an incremental migration plan before accepting a core service direction.

likelyOwner.reason: They can clarify the proposed boundary and supply current-source evidence, while a repository-area owner should make the final architecture decision.
